correctness.rationale: Hübener et al. §II Lemma 1 applies to the nonzero symmetric complex multilinear form for n≥4 and forces proportional local factors at every maximum, not merely the existence of a symmetric maximizer. For any interior latitude both Dicke amplitudes are nonzero, and the phase of their ratio is (n−2)φ up to sign. The only optimal phases modulo 2π are 2πj/(n−2). The two poles have zero overlap. With x=(1+tanh t)/2, the phase-maximized squared overlap is n·2^(1−n) cosh²(at)/coshⁿ(t), a=(n−2)/2. For a>1 the logarithmic derivative of tanh(at)/tanh t is negative by sinh(2at)>a sinh(2t), so the ratio strictly decreases from a to 1 on t>0. Comparing with n/(n−2) proves no positive root for n=5 and exactly one for n≥6, with the indicated change from increasing to decreasing. For n=4 the log-overlap derivative is −2 tanh t. This gives the complete latitude and phase counts. At n=6, z=tanh t gives z²=1/3, cosh(2t)=2 and cosh⁶t=27/8, hence 2/9. On x≤1/2 the contribution squared of the minority Dicke term is at most 2^(−n), using x(1−x)≤1/4, while the dominant term is bounded by its value at x=1/n; symmetry and testing x=1/n give the same limiting lower and upper bound 1/(2e). The inspected verifier was not executed; its finite grids do not establish this optimizer classification.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These results remove the tensor and phase optimization for the value, but do not solve the remaining parameter-dependent scalar problem or count all its maximizing rays. The strict monotonicity across all n supplies the additional conclusion.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The remaining classification does not follow by substituting n into a solved prior formula: the crossing and uniqueness needed at unbounded n and the asymptotic bound are additional arguments. The early cases are consistency checks, not separate discoveries.

evidence: The same states occur as complementary Dicke pairs, and their Majorana sets are an equatorial regular (n−2)-gon and two poles. Aulbach–Markham–Murao write the exact five- and seven-qubit states and rotate the minus-sign octahedron presentation to the positive six-qubit state. Ψ₄=(X⊗I⊗I⊗I)H⊗⁴ GHZ₄.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In these equivalent forms the special cases are genuinely covered. Logarithmic geometric entanglement log₂(1/Λ²) has to be converted to 1−Λ² for comparison.

evidence: The primary case study gives three equatorial closest products and log₂(16/5) for n=5, eight cube-face-direction closest products and log₂(9/2) for n=6, and ten closest products on two circles for n=7. The same-day Resultary record b23c11a55197 studies QFI under phase damping for the identical state; the other two records concern a single W state and an incoherent mixed Dicke-edge state, respectively.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The exact small cases, including the six-qubit overlap and both latitudes, are covered, not merely suggested. Neither the cited exact cases nor the other catalogue observables determine the all-n theorem.

originality.rationale: Pass is for the uniform all-n classification and limit. The scalar optimization framework and the individual n=4,5,6,7 cases must not be counted as novel: the four-qubit state is locally equivalent to GHZ, and Aulbach–Markham–Murao treat the same tri-, square-, and pentagonal dipyramid states. Those examples already show the observed switch from equatorial rays to two circles at six qubits; they do not prove the two-latitude branch persists at every larger n or the limit. The same-day Resultary hit uses the same state but a different observable. No inspected statement covers the uniform branch theorem.
residual_risks: An unlocated general solution under an alternative symmetric tensor or Majorana dipyramid formulation remains possible. The individual case overlap is verified, not merely a risk.
